calculations.equation: osi_approved = count(entry in licenses where entry.isOsiApproved is true); total = count(licenses)

inputs.name: per-entry OSI approval flag
inputs.value: isOsiApproved boolean present on catalogue entries

calculations.output: 149 of 727 catalogue entries carry isOsiApproved true
calculations.uncertainty: Exact integer count over one fixed artefact; it is reproducible byte-for-byte from the recorded SHA-256 and carries no sampling error. It is not a count of all OSI-approved licences in the world, only of those catalogued in this SPDX edition.

calculations.equation: llama_entries = count(entry in licenses where 'llama' is a substring of lowercase(entry.name concatenated with entry.licenseId))
calculations.uncertainty: A case-insensitive substring test can only miss an entry catalogued under a name containing neither the string llama nor that string in its identifier. A null count is evidence of absence from this catalogue, not proof that approval was sought and refused.

counterevidence.claim: Meta's own repository presents Llama as open source.
counterevidence.evidence: Llama is an accessible, open large language model (LLM) designed for developers, researchers, and businesses to build, experiment, and responsibly scale their generative AI ideas. The same README states: The model weights are licensed for researchers and commercial entities, upholding the principles of openness.
counterevidence.qualification: This cuts against the framing of the audited claim rather than against its verdict. The repository README never uses the phrase open source; it uses open, open access and principles of openness. Attributing the exact phrase open source to this repository is unsupported by the retrieved text. Meta statements published elsewhere were not retrievable here and are recorded as unresolved.

counterevidence.claim: Absence from the SPDX catalogue establishes that the licence was assessed and rejected.
counterevidence.qualification: Retained against the audit's own result. The catalogue records licences submitted and processed; a licence may be absent because no one submitted it. The null count is therefore evidence of non-membership only, and result-2 is stated at that strength.

dependencies.description: Every approval finding rests on one third-party catalogue. SPDX records licences it has processed; a licence can be absent because it was never submitted rather than because it was assessed and rejected.

The licence text audited is the copy distributed in the GitHub repository at one pinned commit. The agreement itself incorporates an externally hosted policy page, so the operative terms are split across a carrier not retrieved here.

Open source is operationalised here as presence in the SPDX-recorded OSI-approved set, because the Open Source Definition text itself was not retrievable in this environment. A different operationalisation could reach a different verdict.

The total count, the approval count and the null Llama count are all derived from a single artefact by the same parser, so they share one retrieval and one parsing root and are not three independent observations.

Both licence texts were retrieved from the same repository at the same commit in one session, so the cross-version agreement of the user-count gate is a single retrieval event, not independent corroboration.

license.source_material: Each source retains its own recorded licence. The SPDX catalogue is CC0-1.0; the Meta texts remain under their respective Llama Community License Agreements and are quoted only in quote-minimal spans for audit.

limitations: The provider-model identity behind this run is withheld by the operating policy of the environment and is recorded as unknown. Any assessment of independence between this submission and another must therefore treat model identity as unresolved rather than as distinct.

Network egress was restricted to GitHub and package registries, so no source outside those hosts could be retrieved. The audit is built only from what that restriction allowed, and the criterion source is a casualty of it.
The audit reads licence text. It is not legal advice and makes no claim about how any clause would be construed or enforced.
The comparison target is a catalogue property, not the Open Source Definition itself, so the verdict is precisely as strong as the SPDX approval flag and no stronger.
Only the Llama 3.1 and Llama 4 licences were examined; other licences in the same repository were not audited and are not covered by any result.

lineage.retrieval_environment: Ephemeral container with HTTPS egress restricted by policy to GitHub hosts and public package registries; all other hosts refused at the proxy.
shared_dependencies: All five artefacts were retrieved by one agent in one session over one network path, so they share a single retrieval root and give no independent corroboration of each other.
The two Meta licence texts and the policy and README come from one repository at one commit, so they share a single publisher and a single revision root.
All three calculations were executed by one parser in one process, so they share a method root and a runtime root.
Provider-model identity is withheld, so no claim of independence from any other run can be supported.

question: Does the Llama 4 Community License qualify as an open-source license by the SPDX-recorded OSI-approval test, and what field-of-use and branding conditions does its own text place on redistribution?

results.interpretation: This is a licensee-identity condition rather than a use condition: the same act of redistribution is permitted for a small licensee and withheld from a large one. The identical clause in the Llama 3.1 text shows it is a standing feature of the licence family, not a one-release artefact.
results.proposition: The Llama 4 Community License withholds all granted rights from any licensee whose products exceeded 700 million monthly active users in the calendar month preceding the release date, unless Meta separately grants a licence at its sole discretion.

reported_value.comparison: licensee monthly active users in the preceding calendar month against the 700000000 threshold

results.uncertainty: The clause is quoted exactly, so its existence is not in doubt. Whether it has ever been enforced, and against whom, is unmeasured here.
results.warrant: Section 2 of each licence states the threshold, the measurement window and the discretionary-grant requirement in terms that need no interpretation beyond reading.

results.interpretation: By the SPDX-recorded OSI-approval test the Llama licences are not open-source licences: they are not in the approved subset, and they are not in the catalogue at all. Because the catalogue postdates both releases, the absence is not explained by the catalogue being older than the licences.
results.proposition: No licence bearing the Llama name appears anywhere in SPDX License List v3.28.0, whose 727 catalogued entries include 149 recorded as OSI-approved, and whose release date of 2026-02-20 postdates both the Llama 3.1 and Llama 4 releases.

results.uncertainty: Absence from a catalogue is weaker evidence than a recorded rejection. This result establishes non-membership, not that any body assessed and refused the licence.

results.interpretation: These are conditions on who may use the material and for what, and on how downstream products must be branded, rather than the notice-preservation conditions typical of permissive redistribution licences. The field-of-endeavour bar is the condition most directly in tension with the ordinary meaning of the open-source label.
results.proposition: The Llama 4 licence conditions redistribution on displaying a Meta-specified notice, on prefixing the names of derived models, and on adherence to an incorporated policy that bars named fields of endeavour including military, warfare, nuclear and espionage applications.

search_notes: Sources were restricted to artefacts retrievable at immutable pinned references: a repository commit identifier for the Meta texts and a release tag for the SPDX catalogue, so that a reviewer resolves the same bytes.
Every artefact was retrieved twice and its SHA-256 compared across retrievals; all five hashes were stable, so the recorded digests identify re-retrievable content rather than one transient response.

Retrieval of the definition texts and of the canonical policy page was attempted before the method was operationalised through SPDX, and those failures are recorded as negative results rather than omitted.
The SPDX counts were computed locally over the hashed artefact rather than read from any summary page, so a reviewer can recompute them from the digest alone.
